subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
THE FORWARD BRANCH-PAIR'S PRECONDITION IS AN EPILOGUE TARGET, NOT MERELY A SHARED BLOCK. claim.law.empty-block-branch-pair-splits-forward-vs-backedge.20260831.v1 establishes the important half of this -- the forward variant of `bCOND <next insn>` + `b <far label>` is source-reachable while the backedge variant never is -- and states the reproducible spelling as 'a guard whose body is a SINGLE control transfer to a block that is genuinely reached from elsewhere too'. That stated precondition is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and taking it as sufficient costs probes. Measured here on three forward-variant sites in one function, all of which already satisfy it and none of which reproduces the pair under any spelling: the guard bodies transfer to interior labels that ARE reached from elsewhere (a `goto` label whose fallthrough predecessor also reaches it, and a `continue` target reached by three sibling guards), and MWCC still canonicalises every spelling to the single inverted branch. What the law's own two positive controls actually share, and what the failing sites lack, is that the transfer targets the FUNCTION EPILOGUE -- OSRtc.c::ReadSram's body is `return 0;` and atree.c::AtreeFindNodeIdx's is `return i;`. That is exactly the boundary claim.law.DE_merged-disjunction-unfuses-a-forward-guard-pair-only-into-the-epilogue.20260901.v1 states for the merged-disjunction lever, and this record's contribution is to show the SAME boundary binds the empty-block branch-pair family, on a different micro-shape (an integer `bge`/`b` clamp guard, not a disjunction) and at a site no prior record had screened. Read the two laws as one boundary: a return targets a block the front end has already materialised; an interior label does not, however many predecessors it has.

WHAT WAS PROBED, SO IT IS NOT RE-PROBED. Two source spellings, chosen to attack the two directions the family suggests, both byte-identical. (1) DE MORGAN, moving the transfer INSIDE the guard so the body is a single control transfer exactly as the empty-block law prescribes: `if (A && B) { continue; } goto L;` rewritten as `if (!A || !B) { goto L; }`. (2) BLOCK-BODIED POSITIVE GUARD, replacing an explicitly single-branch negated goto with the statement block it guards: `if (x < 0) { goto L; } BODY; L:` rewritten as `if (x >= 0) { BODY }`. Neither moved a byte. The generalisation worth carrying is that MWCC's front end normalises guard POLARITY and guard SPELLING to one inverted branch before any pass that could split it, so the branch pair is not a spelling choice at all -- it is a property of what the body targets.

SCREEN CHEAPLY, IN THIS ORDER. Before spending a probe on a target-only `b` next to a conditional: (a) confirm the variant is FORWARD, per the parent law, since the backedge half is dead; (b) confirm the guard body's transfer reaches the EPILOGUE -- a `return`, or a goto to a label whose only content is the return path. If it reaches an interior label, the site is closed and no spelling will open it. (c) Only then check peephole, and check it by reading the TU's actual cflags rather than assuming: a TU on cflags_demo already has peephole off, so a surviving pair in the target is not evidence for a flag change and no flag work is owed.
